subproblem.title: Positive antitone null scales adapted to a given real sequence
subproblem.statement: Let a : ℕ → ℝ be an arbitrary real sequence. Then there is a sequence ρ : ℕ → ℝ such that ρ_k > 0 for every k ∈ ℕ, ρ is antitone (ρ_l ≤ ρ_k whenever k ≤ l), ρ_k → 0 as k → ∞, and ρ_k·a_k ≤ 1/(k+1) for every k ∈ ℕ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, ∃ ρ : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, 0 < ρ k) ∧ Antitone ρ ∧ Tendsto ρ atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ k, ρ k * a k ≤ 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 (Scales) of the parent proof, which chooses the scales ρ_k ↓ 0 of Simon 6.2 according to the masses. The parent applies this with a_k = (M(X_k) + M(∂X_k)).toReal ≥ 0. Here a_k is arbitrary, so 1 + a_k is replaced by b_k := 1 + |a_k|; this equals 1 + a_k when a_k ≥ 0, giving exactly the parent's construction.

1. Put b_k := 1 + |a_k|. Then b_k ≥ 1 > 0 for every k.
2. Define ρ recursively: ρ_0 := 1/b_0 and ρ_{j+1} := min{ρ_j, 1/((j+2)·b_{j+1})} for j ∈ ℕ. (In Lean, use Nat.rec; both defining equations then hold by rfl.)
3. (Positivity.) By induction on k.
   - ρ_0 = 1/b_0 > 0.
   - If ρ_j > 0, then ρ_{j+1} is the minimum of ρ_j > 0 and 1/((j+2)·b_{j+1}) > 0, hence positive (lt_min).
4. (Antitone.) ρ_{j+1} ≤ ρ_j for every j (min_le_left), so ρ is antitone (antitone_nat_of_succ_le).
5. (Upper bound.) For every k, ρ_k ≤ 1/((k+1)·b_k).
   - For k = 0: ρ_0 = 1/b_0 = 1/((0+1)·b_0).
   - For k = j+1: ρ_{j+1} ≤ 1/((j+2)·b_{j+1}) (min_le_right). Moreover (j+1)+1 = j+2; for the casts ℕ → ℝ, ((j+1 : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 = (j : ℝ) + 2 (push_cast, ring).
6. (Limit.)
   - Since b_k ≥ 1, (k+1)·b_k ≥ k+1 > 0. So step 5 gives ρ_k ≤ 1/((k+1)·b_k) ≤ 1/(k+1) (one_div_le_one_div_of_le).
   - Thus 0 < ρ_k ≤ 1/(k+1) for all k, and 1/(k+1) → 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat). By the squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero), ρ_k → 0.
7. (Product bound.) Fix k.
   - Since ρ_k > 0 and a_k ≤ |a_k|: ρ_k·a_k ≤ ρ_k·|a_k|.
   - By step 5 and |a_k| ≥ 0: ρ_k·|a_k| ≤ |a_k|/((k+1)·b_k).
   - Since 0 ≤ |a_k| ≤ 1 + |a_k| = b_k and (k+1)·b_k > 0: |a_k|/((k+1)·b_k) ≤ b_k/((k+1)·b_k) = 1/(k+1).
   - Hence ρ_k·a_k ≤ 1/(k+1).
Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 give the four required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: ρ_k > 0 by induction; ρ is antitone because ρ_{j+1} ≤ ρ_j.

audit.reason: The exact type matches the arbitrary-real-sequence statement. Using 1 + |a_k| handles negative terms. The recursive minimum proves positivity, antitonicity, the reciprocal upper bound and convergence; the final inequalities prove the required product bound. No circular dependency or deferred construction remains.

subproblem.title: Every test form has a finite Euclidean coefficient sup norm
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set and let ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (a TestFormOn U n: a smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞), compactly supported n-form on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ U). Then there is a real number C > 0 such that |ω(x)| ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is Simon's Euclidean coefficient norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x : Eucl P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof: a test form is continuous with compact support, so the supremum of its Euclidean coefficient norm is finite (Simon Ch. 6, 1.15 and 2.4). Here this finiteness is proved directly for the real function x ↦ |ω(x)|, using continuity of |·| rather than the comparison |α| ≤ √N·‖α‖ with the operator norm. The conclusion is the same.

Notation. Λⁿ := Covector (Eucl P) n is the normed space of continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ. For α ∈ Λⁿ, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})² else 0)).

1. (|·| is continuous on Λⁿ.)
   - For each fixed v ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ, the evaluation α ↦ α(v) is continuous on Λⁿ (continuous_eval_const, via the instance ContinuousAlternatingMap.instContinuousEvalConst).
   - Hence for each I : Fin n → Fin P, the summand α ↦ (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})² else 0) is continuous. It is either the square of a continuous function or the constant 0.
   - A finite sum of continuous functions is continuous (continuous_finsetSum), and the square root is continuous (Real.continuous_sqrt). So α ↦ |α| is continuous.
2. (Continuity of f.) ω is smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞, the first component of the test-form property of ω), hence continuous. Therefore f(x) := |ω(x)| is continuous on ℝ^P, as a composition of continuous maps.
3. (Compact support of f.)
   - If ω(x) = 0 then f(x) = |0| = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). Hence support f ⊆ support ω ⊆ tsupport ω.
   - ω has compact support (the second component of IsTestForm), so f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono').
4. (Boundedness.) A continuous, compactly supported real function is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support): there is C₀ ∈ ℝ with ‖f(x)‖ ≤ C₀ for all x ∈ ℝ^P. In particular C₀ ≥ ‖f(0)‖ ≥ 0.
5. Put C := C₀ + 1. Then C ≥ 1 > 0, and for every x ∈ ℝ^P, f(x) ≤ |f(x)| = ‖f(x)‖ ≤ C₀ < C. So |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x. ∎
proof_key_steps: covectorEuclideanNorm is continuous on Λⁿ: continuous evaluations, a finite sum of squares, and the square root.
f(x) = |ω(x)| is continuous because ω is smooth.
f has compact support because |0| = 0 and ω has compact support.
A continuous compactly supported real function is bounded by some C₀ ≥ 0; take C = C₀ + 1 > 0.

audit.reason: The statement correctly covers arbitrary U and all degrees. Continuous covector evaluations give continuity of the coefficient norm; its zero value preserves compact support. Compact-support boundedness and C = C₀ + 1 supply the positive bound. No openness hypothesis or additional lemma is missing.

subproblem.title: Flat decompositions with vanishing masses give pointwise convergence of the differences
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set. For k ∈ ℕ let X_k, Pc_k, S_k ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R_k ∈ D_{n+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (n+1)). Assume X_k(ω) − Pc_k(ω) = ∂R_k(ω) + S_k(ω) for every k ∈ ℕ and every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U). Assume also M(R_k) → 0 and M(S_k) → 0 in [0, ∞] as k → ∞, where M(·) = mass = M_U(·). Then Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) → 0 as k → ∞ for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (X Pc S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)), (∀ (k : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn U n), X k ω - Pc k ω = (R k).boundary ω + S k ω) → Tendsto (fun k => (R k).mass) atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun k => (S k).mass) atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Tendsto (fun k => Pc k ω - X k ω) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 6.2, printed proof (p. 169). It has (1) T − P_k = ∂R_k + S_k and (2) M(R_k) ≤ cρ_kM(T) → 0, M(S_k) ≤ cρ_kM(∂T) → 0, followed by 'Evidently (1), (2) give P_k(ω) → T(ω)'; the printed 'T_k(ω)' is a misprint for T(ω). This is step 6 of the parent proof, written for sequences X_k, Pc_k and an arbitrary set U. It uses two sibling lemmas:
- mass_estimate: |Y(η)| ≤ C·M(Y).toReal whenever C > 0, |η(x)| ≤ C for all x, and M(Y) ≠ ∞.
- testform_bounded: every test form η has some C > 0 with |η(x)| ≤ C for all x.

Notation: |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α and M(Y) = Y.mass.

1. Fix ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) and put dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U n ω ∈ D^{n+1}(U). By the definition of the boundary (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), ∂R_k(ω) = R_k(dω) for every k. So the hypothesis reads X_k(ω) − Pc_k(ω) = R_k(dω) + S_k(ω), i.e. Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) = −(R_k(dω) + S_k(ω)) for every k.
2. By testform_bounded, in degree n for ω and in degree n+1 for dω, choose C₀ > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ C₀ for all x ∈ ℝ^P, and C₁ > 0 with |dω(x)| ≤ C₁ for all x ∈ ℝ^P.
3. (Finiteness and real limits.)
   - Since M(R_k) → 0 and 0 ≠ ∞, the set {t ∈ [0, ∞] : t ≠ ∞} is a neighbourhood of 0 (eventually_ne_nhds). So M(R_k) ≠ ∞ for all sufficiently large k. Likewise M(S_k) ≠ ∞ for all sufficiently large k.
   - ENNReal.toReal is continuous at 0 ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), and (0 : [0, ∞]).toReal = 0. Hence M(R_k).toReal → 0 and M(S_k).toReal → 0 in ℝ.
4. (Estimate.) Let k be large enough that M(R_k) ≠ ∞ and M(S_k) ≠ ∞; by step 3 this holds for all sufficiently large k.
   - mass_estimate with Y = R_k, form dω and constant C₁ gives |R_k(dω)| ≤ C₁·M(R_k).toReal.
   - mass_estimate with Y = S_k, form ω and constant C₀ gives |S_k(ω)| ≤ C₀·M(S_k).toReal.
   - With step 1 and the triangle inequality: |Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω)| = |R_k(dω) + S_k(ω)| ≤ |R_k(dω)| + |S_k(ω)| ≤ C₁·M(R_k).toReal + C₀·M(S_k).toReal.
5. (Squeeze.) By step 3, the right-hand side C₁·M(R_k).toReal + C₀·M(S_k).toReal tends to C₁·0 + C₀·0 = 0 (Tendsto.const_mul, Tendsto.add). The bound of step 4 holds for all sufficiently large k, so the squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero_norm', with ‖r‖ = |r| on ℝ) gives Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) → 0. Since ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) was arbitrary, the claim follows. ∎
proof_key_steps: testform_bounded gives C₀, C₁ > 0 bounding |ω| and |dω| everywhere.
M(R_k) and M(S_k) are eventually finite, and their toReal values tend to 0.
mass_estimate gives |Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω)| ≤ C₁·M(R_k).toReal + C₀·M(S_k).toReal eventually.

audit.reason: The prose and type agree on degrees, domain, decomposition and ENNReal limits. Exterior differentiation preserves TestFormOn for arbitrary U. Convergence to zero gives eventual finiteness and convergence of toReal masses. The two declared siblings yield the eventual evaluation bound, and norm squeezing proves the exact signed difference limit. The proof needs no additional hypotheses or parent theorem.
